questions.question: Who wrote the book 'Unhappy India' as a reply to the biased views of journalist Katherine Mayo?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lala Lajpat Rai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book **'Unhappy India'** was written by **Lala Lajpat Rai** in **1928**. This work served as a systematic and scathing rebuttal to **'Mother India'**, a book published in **1927** by the **American** journalist **Katherine Mayo**. **Hence, option 1 is correct.**
 
• **Katherine Mayo's** book was widely regarded by Indians as **British propaganda**. It focused exclusively on the social pathologies of India, such as **child marriage**, **untouchability**, and **sanitation** issues, to argue that Indians were culturally backward and unfit for **self-governance**.
 
• In **'Unhappy India'**, **Lala Lajpat Rai** utilized **comparative statistics** and historical data to show that similar social problems existed in **Western countries**, including the **United States** and **England**. He argued that the **British colonial administration** was largely responsible for the economic and social stagnation of the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• **Rajendra Prasad**, who later became the **first President of India**, authored the book **'India Divided'** in **1946**, which analyzed the **Two-Nation Theory** and the demand for **Pakistan**. **Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.**
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal** was a revolutionary leader and a brilliant orator often called the **'Father of Revolutionary Thoughts'**, but he was not the author of this specific reply to Mayo. **Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.**
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, a prominent nationalist leader, wrote **'The Arctic Home in the Vedas'** and **'Gita Rahasya'** (written during his imprisonment in **Mandalay**), but he passed away in **1920**, years before Mayo's book was published. **Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai** (born **January 28, 1865**) was a legendary freedom fighter from **Punjab**, earned the titles **'Punjab Kesari'** and **'Sher-e-Punjab'** (Lion of Punjab). He was a key figure in the **Lal-Bal-Pal** trio of the **Extremist** faction of the **Indian National Congress**.
 
• He was a staunch follower of **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** and played a pivotal role in the expansion of the **Arya Samaj** in **North India**. He also co-founded the **Punjab National Bank** in **1894** and the **Lakshmi Insurance Company**.
 
• **Katherine Mayo's** **'Mother India'** caused such an international stir that **Mahatma Gandhi** reviewed it in **'Young India'**, famously labeling it a **'Drain Inspector's Report'** because it focused only on the filth and ignored the beauty of the nation.
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai** was also the **President** of the **Indian National Congress** during the **Calcutta Special Session** in **1920**, where the **Non-Cooperation Movement** was first discussed.
 
• He founded the **Servants of the People Society** in **1921**, a non-profit welfare organization aimed at training national missionaries for service to the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Martyrdom**: In **October 1928**, **Lala Lajpat Rai** led a massive protest against the **Simon Commission** in **Lahore**. During the demonstration, he was severely injured in a **lathi charge** sanctioned by the British police superintendent **James A. Scott**.
 
• He famously declared, **'Every blow on my body will prove a nail in the coffin of the British Empire.'** He passed away on **November 17, 1928**, due to the injuries sustained.
 
• **Retaliation**: His death deeply affected the young revolutionaries of the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)**. **Bhagat Singh**, **Shivaram Rajguru**, and **Sukhdev Thapar** vowed to avenge his death, leading to the **Lahore Conspiracy Case** and the assassination of **John P. Saunders** in **December 1928**.
 
• **Literary Contributions**: Apart from **'Unhappy India'**, his other significant writings include **'Young India: An Interpretation and a History of the Nationalist Movement from Within'** and **'The Story of My Deportation'**.

questions.question: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus is located in which of the following city?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT)** is a historic terminal train station and a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** located in the city of **Mumbai**, **Maharashtra**, **India**.
 
• It serves as the headquarters of the **Central Railway**, one of the **19 zones** of the **Indian Railways**.
 
• The station was designed by the **British** architectural engineer **Frederick William Stevens**, who worked on the project for ten years starting in **1878**.
 
• It is a prime example of **Victorian Gothic Revival** architecture in **India**, which also incorporates elements of **Indian traditional architecture**, such as the stone dome, turrets, and pointed arches.
 
• The station is the correct answer as it is a landmark synonymous with **Mumbai**; other options like **Kolkata**, **Delhi**, and **Ahmadabad** have their own primary terminals such as **Howrah Junction**, **New Delhi Railway Station**, and **Ahmedabad Junction** respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The station was originally named **Victoria Terminus (VT)** to commemorate the **Golden Jubilee** of **Queen Victoria** in **1887**.
 
• In **1996**, the station was renamed **Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus** in honor of the founder of the **Maratha Empire**, **Chhatrapati Shivaji**. The word **Maharaj** was later added to the name in **July 2017**.
 
• The architectural style is often described as **Indo-Saracenic**, featuring a blend of **Western** and **Eastern** influences, including wood carvings, ornamental iron, and brass railings.
 
• The building is constructed from a mix of **light-colored sandstone** and **grey basalt**, with **Italian marble** used for some of the interior decorative elements.
 
• It is one of the busiest railway stations in the world, serving as a hub for both long-distance trains and the **Mumbai Suburban Railway**, which carries millions of passengers every day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The site where **CSMT** stands today was originally known as **Bori Bunder**, which was the location of the first railway station in **India**.
 
• The first passenger train in **India** departed from **Bori Bunder** to **Thane** on **April 16, 1853**, covering a distance of **34 kilometers**.
 
• The station has **18 platforms** in total; platforms **1 to 7** are utilized for **Suburban** local trains, while platforms **8 to 18** are used for **Main Line** outstation trains.
 
• The **UNESCO** recognition was granted in **2004**, citing the station as an outstanding example of the meeting of two cultures, as **British** architects worked with **Indian** craftsmen to create a unique architectural style.
 
• The central dome of the building is topped by a **colossal figure** of a woman holding a torch pointing upwards, symbolizing **Progress**.

Nobody wants to part _______ their money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**with**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The phrasal verb **'part with'** is an idiomatic expression that means to **give up possession** of something, especially something that you would prefer to keep or that is valuable.

• In the context of the sentence, **'money'** is a possession that people are often reluctant to give away, making **'with'** the grammatically correct preposition.

• The phrase **'part from'** is typically used when referring to **separating from a person** or leaving someone's company (e.g., 'He was sad to part from his friends').

• Options like **'on'** and **'away'** do not form standard idiomatic collocations with the verb **'part'** to convey the meaning of giving something up.

**Additional Information__**

• **Prepositions** are words that show the relationship between a noun or pronoun and other words in a sentence.

• **Fixed Prepositions** are specific prepositions that are always used with certain verbs, adjectives, or nouns to convey a particular meaning.

• Example of **'part with'**: 'She found it hard to **part with** her childhood toys.'

• Example of **'part from'**: 'The travelers **parted from** each other at the crossroads.'
</ul

The children ate pancakes _______ burgers for breakfast today.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**instead of**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The prepositional phrase **instead of** is used to indicate that one person, thing, or action **replaces** or is chosen in preference to another.

• In the given sentence, **pancakes** were eaten as a **substitute** for **burgers**, making **instead of** the logically correct choice.

• **Option 2 (because of)** and **Option 3 (owing to)** are used to indicate a **reason** or **cause**. They do not fit here because burgers are not the cause of eating pancakes.

• **Option 4 (again)** is an **adverb** meaning 'once more'. It cannot function as a **preposition** to connect the two nouns 'pancakes' and 'burgers' in this context.

**Additional Information__**

• **Instead of** is a **compound preposition** that is typically followed by a **noun**, **pronoun**, or a **gerund** (the -ing form of a verb).

• **Owing to** is often used at the beginning of a sentence and is generally considered more **formal** than **because of**.

• **Prepositions** are essential parts of speech that establish **relationships** in time, space, or logic between different elements of a sentence.
</ul

• Options such as **up**, **for**, and **about** do not form standard idiomatic expressions with the word **deprived** and therefore result in an incorrect sentence structure.

• The term **downtrodden** describes people who are **oppressed**, **subjugated**, or treated unfairly by those in positions of authority.

</ul
